terra.problem: The passage does not mention a dinner invitation. Marking Peter's feeling as a guess does not establish that an invitation occurred.
Saying Peter trusts his story attributes an unstated feeling to him.
“A large sheet it was” turns Peter's comparison into a definite identification. He says it was something like a large sheet.
Joppa being a seaside town is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
“Just a big sheet” drops Peter's qualification that it was something like a sheet.
The explanation is a flat restatement of the answer, with little of Papa Dorin's voice.
“An easy morning” gives the event a time of day that the passage does not supply.
The explanation repeats the answer in a generic way without adding much personality or insight.
Peter going to Caesarea is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
“No waiting around” and the contrast with waiting until morning imply an immediate departure. Acts 10:23 says the men stayed as Peter's guests and they left the next day.
Identifying the man as Cornelius draws on Acts 10, outside this passage, and needs a reference.
